title: Letter and Parish Revisited
premise: Ivo Halloran, a night-shift dispatcher who has quietly catalogued the town of Saltmere's secrets for twelve years, receives a prepaid booking from a nervous woman asking to be driven somewhere at 3 a.m. — and to be told if anyone follows. When she vanishes before the pickup, Ivo discovers her payment was made in the name of Ellen Voss, a girl who drowned twelve years ago in the case the whole parish swore was an accident. Following the woman's trail through his own meticulous records, Ivo realizes Ellen didn't drown: she survived, reinvented herself, and has returned because someone is about to kill again to keep the original crime buried. In the end, Ivo must choose between turning over his files — which would expose his own years of complicit silence — or letting the tide take the truth; he burns the ledger but testifies, giving Ellen a new name and himself a smaller, honest life.
about_author: Isandro Blackwood spent a decade working night dispatch for coastal transport companies before turning to fiction, a job he credits with teaching him how much people confess to strangers on the phone. He writes mysteries from a rented room above a shuttered chandlery, where the fog arrives earlier than the news does.

chapters.title: The Prepaid Fare
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV. A routine night shift breaks pattern when a client books a 3 a.m. ride under the name of Ellen Voss — a girl officially dead for twelve years — then never appears. Digging into his dispatch logs, Ivo finds three other bookings under dead parishioners' names across the past month. The emotional beat is unease curdling into obsession as the man who alphabetizes secrets realizes one has been filed under his own nose.

chapters.title: What the Tide Kept
chapters.summary: Alternating between Ivo's present investigation and fragmented recollections of the night Ellen Voss went into the water. Ivo tracks the living woman to a caravan park and confronts her: she is Ellen, disfigured and renamed, back because the man who pushed her that night — now a respected parish councillor — is closing loose ends. The beat is dread and reluctant alliance as two survivors of the same lie agree to build a case outside the law.

chapters.title: Twelve Years of Silence
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, rising tension. As Ellen baits the councillor with staged evidence, Ivo discovers his own predecessor dispatcher helped bury the original cover-up — meaning his beloved archive is itself evidence of complicity. The councillor, alerted, comes for the ledgers; Ivo barely escapes with the key pages as the depot burns. The beat is betrayal and reckoning: the system Ivo trusted was the crime's quietest accomplice.

chapters.title: Low Water
chapters.summary: Ivo's POV, climax and resolution. At the tidal causeway where Ellen 'drowned,' the councillor corners them to finish what he started; Ivo trades his silence for a recorded confession as the water rises, forcing a standoff resolved by the incoming tide and arriving police tipped off by Ivo's final dispatch call. In the aftermath, Ivo burns his secret archive, keeps only the pages that matter, and watches Ellen board a bus under a name no one has ever filed away.
